title: Junk Furniture Removal in Hampton Roads: 8 Things to Know Before You Call
excerpt: Learn what to expect with junk furniture removal in Hampton Roads: pricing, item eligibility, eco-disposal, DIY costs, and local triggers like PCS moves.
metaTitle: Junk Furniture Removal in Hampton Roads Guide
metaDescription: Learn what to expect with junk furniture removal in Hampton Roads: pricing, item eligibility, eco-disposal, DIY costs, and local triggers like PCS moves.
contentHtml:
So you've got an old couch taking up half your living room, a broken dresser that's been sitting in the corner for months, or maybe an entire room full of furniture you just don't need anymore. Sound familiar? You're definitely not alone. Getting rid of bulky furniture is one of those tasks that feels way more complicated than it should be.

That's where junk furniture removal services come in, and if you live in the Hampton Roads area, you've got some solid options available to you. But before you grab your phone and start calling around, there are a few things worth knowing that can save you time, money, and a whole lot of headaches.

Whether you're clearing out after a move, downsizing, or just finally tackling that cluttered spare room, this guide is here to help. We're breaking down eight important things every Hampton Roads homeowner should understand before scheduling a pickup. From pricing to what companies will and won't take, consider this your beginner-friendly roadmap to getting that unwanted furniture out of your life for good.

What Actually Counts as Junk Furniture

Before you schedule a pickup, it helps to know exactly what falls under the junk furniture removal umbrella. The good news is that most of the bulky stuff cluttering your home qualifies without any problem.

Standard accepted items cover a wide range, including sofas, sectionals, recliners, loveseats, mattresses, box springs, bed frames, dressers, dining tables and chairs, desks, office chairs, bookshelves, entertainment centers, and outdoor patio furniture. If it used to serve a purpose in your home and it no longer does, there's a strong chance a removal crew can haul it away in a single visit.

Large appliances are a bit of a gray area. Refrigerators, washers, dryers, and dishwashers often fall within the scope of furniture removal services, but you should always confirm before scheduling. Refrigerators and freezers containing Freon may require special handling prior to transport, which can affect pricing. According to Waste Management's household hazardous waste guidance, certain materials require care beyond standard collection, so a quick call to confirm appliance acceptance saves you from surprises on removal day.

What crews will not take includes hazardous materials such as paint, chemicals, asbestos-containing materials, propane tanks, and medical waste. The EPA classifies products like paints, cleaners, oils, and pesticides as household hazardous waste requiring specialized disposal, which falls completely outside standard junk removal.

One of the biggest perks of professional junk furniture removal is the ability to combine items into a single service call. A broken sofa, an old dresser, and a stack of patio chairs can all go out the door at once, saving you from scheduling multiple pickups.

How Junk Furniture Removal Is Priced in Hampton Roads

Pricing is one of the first things people want to know before scheduling a pickup, and the good news is that it's pretty straightforward once you understand how the system works.

Most professional junk removal companies price by volume, meaning the amount of space your items take up in the truck. It's not typically charged by the hour or by how many individual pieces you have. A single heavy recliner might cost less than a lightweight but bulky sectional that eats up half the truck, simply because the sectional takes up more space.

Here's a realistic look at what junk furniture removal costs in the Hampton Roads area:

  • Single large item (one sofa, mattress, or dresser): roughly $75 to $150

  • Partial truckload (a few pieces of furniture, like a bedroom set or a couch plus a couple of chairs): approximately $150 to $300

  • Full truckload: generally $400 to $600, depending on item weight and local disposal fees

According to how much junk removal costs in Hampton Roads, labor alone represents 42% of total junk removal expenses industry-wide. That's a big chunk, and it's one reason why pricing can vary so much from one provider to another. It also explains why some companies surprise customers with extra charges after the truck is already loaded.

Some national franchise operators use variable or tiered fee structures that aren't fully disclosed until the crew shows up. Local providers who offer free, itemized estimates give you a firm number before any work begins, which protects your budget from unexpected add-ons.

The easiest way to know your actual cost before committing? Request a free estimate. Send a few photos of your items or schedule a quick walkthrough call. Mr. Demo Pro offers free estimates for furniture removal throughout Hampton Roads, including Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, and Newport News. You can reach them at 757-848-4559 to get a clear, upfront quote with no surprises.

DIY vs. Professional Removal: The Real Cost Breakdown

A lot of homeowners assume DIY is the obvious budget move when it comes to junk furniture removal. But once you run the actual numbers, that assumption starts to fall apart pretty quickly.

Renting a pickup truck or cargo van in Hampton Roads typically runs $80 to $130 per day before you add mileage charges and fuel. Mileage fees alone can run $0.70 to $1.10 per mile, and a loaded truck gets rough gas mileage. Here's the part most people miss: a typical furniture haul, think a sofa, mattress, dresser, and a few chairs, usually fills more than one load. That means at least two trips to a landfill or transfer station, and every trip adds to your total.

Virginia tipping fees for bulky waste range from $25 to $60 per visit depending on the facility and how much your load weighs. Two trips means doubling that estimate. Most people budget for one and get surprised at the scale house.

There's also a real physical risk that doesn't show up on any receipt. Back strains and crush injuries from moving heavy furniture are among the most common home-related injuries. Standard homeowners insurance policies typically do not cover accidents that happen during DIY moving or hauling, so an ER visit lands entirely on you.

On top of all that, not every Hampton Roads transfer station accepts mattresses or large upholstered furniture on the same day or at the same location. You may need to call ahead, drive to a separate facility, or wait for a scheduled bulky waste day.

When you stack up truck rental, fuel, tipping fees (times two), and a half-day of your time, professional removal often comes in within $50 to $100 of the DIY total. Check out this 2026 junk removal cost breakdown by state to see how the numbers compare in your region. The professional option skips the heavy lifting, the logistics, and the guesswork entirely.

Eco-Friendly Disposal: Where Your Furniture Actually Goes

Here's something worth knowing before you book any removal service: eco-friendly disposal is a genuine purchase driver for most people today. North America leads the global junk removal market largely because of high consumer awareness and demand for green services, and reputable haulers have responded by building real sorting systems into their process.

The Disposal Hierarchy That Responsible Haulers Follow

The best operators follow a clear sequence after your furniture leaves the curb. Usable items go to donation partners first, recyclable materials go to processors second, and only items with absolutely no remaining life end up in a landfill. According to the U.S. EPA, Americans send roughly 146 million tons of waste to landfills every year, which is exactly why this sorting step matters so much.

Where Your Furniture Goes Locally

In Hampton Roads, furniture in good condition gets routed to donation partners like Habitat for Humanity ReStores, with locations across Norfolk, Virginia Beach, and Chesapeake, and Salvation Army, both of which resell furniture to fund community programs. For pieces that cannot be donated, material recycling takes over. Metal frames go to scrap processors, wood components move to appropriate waste streams, and foam and fabric are handled by facilities equipped for upholstered materials.

The Question You Should Always Ask

Ask any hauler directly about their disposal chain: which donation partners they use, their recycling rate, and what percentage actually reaches a landfill. Reputable companies should answer this without hesitation. Since no hauler is legally required to report diversion rates and most figures are self-reported, asking directly is simply smart consumer behavior.

Virginia-Specific Rules for Mattresses and Regulated Items

Not all furniture removal is created equal, and Virginia has its own set of rules that can catch homeowners off guard if they're not prepared. Here are five things you need to know before hauling anything to the curb.

1. Mattresses Have Curbside Restrictions in Hampton Roads

Virginia has no statewide mattress recycling mandate, but individual cities handle this differently. In many Hampton Roads municipalities, you cannot simply drag a mattress to the curb and expect it to disappear. Unpermitted curbside mattress placement can trigger a code violation fine, so always contact your city's public works department to schedule a bulky item pickup before putting anything outside.

2. Electronics Cannot Go Into Standard Removal Loads

Smart TVs, built-in speakers, and similar electronics embedded in furniture setups fall under Virginia's Electronic Waste Recycling Act. These items require separate handling through dedicated programs. The Southeastern Public Service Authority's HHW and E-Waste facilities serve Hampton Roads residents, though drop-offs are capped at five items per visit and require proof of residence. The Virginia DEQ's Universal Waste Requirements govern these disposal obligations at the state level.

3. Appliances With Refrigerants Require Certified Handling

Refrigerators and AC units contain refrigerants that must be recovered by an EPA Section 608-certified technician before disposal. Always confirm your removal provider holds this certification before booking.

4. Pre-1978 Homes May Have Lead Paint or Asbestos

Furniture and composite materials from older renovations may contain lead paint or asbestos. Both fall entirely outside standard junk removal scope and require professional assessment before anyone hauls anything away.

5. Licensing Protects You From Liability

If a regulated item in your load is later found to have been improperly disposed of, liability can fall back on you as the property owner in a DIY scenario. Using a licensed, insured company like Mr. Demo Pro removes that risk entirely. Call 757-848-4559 for a free estimate.

Why Hampton Roads Creates Constant Demand for Furniture Removal

If you've ever wondered why junk furniture removal services stay busy year-round in Hampton Roads, the answer comes down to five specific factors that are unique to this region. This isn't a market that slows down between seasons. It stays active because of who lives here, how they move, and the environment they live in.

Military PCS Moves Keep the Volume High

Naval Station Norfolk is one of the largest naval installations in the world, and Joint Base Langley-Eustis adds thousands more service members to the local population. When PCS orders arrive, they typically give families weeks, not months, to relocate. Selling furniture online takes time you don't have. Donation centers often require drop-offs during limited hours. Professional furniture removal becomes the fastest, most practical solution when the clock is already running.

Rental Turnovers Create Repeat Business

Hampton Roads has a dense and active rental market, partly because military families tend to rent rather than buy. When a tenant moves out, landlords need the unit cleared fast to minimize vacancy time. Abandoned sofas, broken bed frames, and worn-out appliances don't move themselves, and property managers can't wait days for piecemeal pickups.

Estate Cleanouts Require One-Stop Removal

When a family member passes away or transitions to assisted living, the resulting cleanout often involves an entire household worth of furniture. Families coordinating from out of town especially benefit from a single comprehensive service call rather than managing multiple vendors.

Flooding Leaves Furniture That Can't Be Saved

Hampton Roads is one of the most flood-prone metro areas in the country. When storm surge or tidal flooding damages furniture, it typically can't be donated or recycled. Mold growth begins within 24 to 48 hours of water exposure, so fast removal isn't just convenient; it's genuinely necessary for protecting your home.

Post-Renovation Cleanouts Pair Naturally with Demo Work

After a kitchen remodel or bathroom renovation, old cabinets, furniture, and construction debris often pile up together. Booking a service that handles both demolition debris and furniture removal in a single visit is simply more efficient than coordinating two separate contractors. Mr. Demo Pro specializes in exactly this kind of bundled approach, serving homeowners across Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, Newport News, Hampton, and Suffolk. Call 757-848-4559 for a free estimate.

How Bundling Furniture Removal with Demolition Saves You a Service Call

Here's something most homeowners don't realize until it's too late: many junk removal providers will only haul items that are already loose and ready to go. They won't tear out the old cabinets, break up a concrete slab, or demo the garage structure first. That means if your project involves any demolition before the cleanup, you're looking at coordinating two separate vendors, two separate schedules, and two separate bills.

That double-vendor problem adds up fast. Each company applies its own mobilization fee, minimum charge, and access surcharges independently. Construction debris alone carries a typical surcharge of $100 to $250 per load above standard pricing, and that cost hits twice when two crews show up instead of one.

Three scenarios where bundling pays off in Hampton Roads:

  • Garage projects: A garage cleanout paired with slab removal or garage demolition is one of the most common bundled jobs in the region. One crew handles the demo and hauls everything in the same visit.

  • Kitchen and bathroom renovations: Renovation debris and old furniture often come out of the same room. Combining the haul-off with furniture removal from that space into a single trip eliminates a redundant service call.

  • Commercial strip-outs: When a business is vacating a space, office furniture removal and interior demolition need to happen in a coordinated sequence. A single crew visit keeps the general contractor's timeline intact.

This isn't a niche scenario either. Construction debris removal grew 9.2% in 2023 and now represents 22% of total U.S. junk removal activity, which means demolition and junk removal are happening together on a significant share of residential and commercial projects nationwide.

When you call for an estimate, ask one specific question: "Can your crew handle both the furniture removal and any demolition or cleanout work in the same visit?" That single question separates true full-service local providers from haul-only operators. Mr. Demo Pro handles both interior demolition and junk removal across Hampton Roads, including Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, and Newport News, and offers free upfront estimates so you know exactly what you're paying before anyone shows up. Call 757-848-4559 to get started.

What to Expect on Removal Day

Knowing what happens from first call to final haul makes the whole process a lot less stressful. Here is a quick rundown of how removal day typically unfolds, step by step.

1. It starts with a free estimate before anyone shows up. Most professional crews, including the team at Mr. Demo Pro, kick things off with a no-cost quote. You can usually do this by phone while sending a few photos, or by scheduling a quick in-person walkthrough. During that conversation, the provider confirms whether your items are eligible for pickup, locks in a firm price, and sets your pickup window. No surprises when the truck rolls up.

2. Same-day and next-day scheduling is now the norm. For single-item pickups or small residential loads, same-day or next-day availability has become a standard expectation across the industry. If you are clearing out a full estate, a commercial space, or a multi-room home, expect the provider to schedule a dedicated half-day or full-day crew block instead.

3. The crew handles every bit of the heavy work. Once the team arrives, your only job is to point at what goes. A professional full-service junk removal crew handles all lifting, loading, and hauling. If a large sectional sofa cannot fit through a doorway intact, they will disassemble it on the spot. Good operators also use floor coverings and doorframe padding to protect your home during the haul-out.

4. Budget 30 to 60 minutes for a standard residential pickup. A few pieces of furniture typically take under an hour from crew arrival to truck departure. Full-home cleanouts or commercial jobs run closer to two to four hours depending on volume and access.

5. Ask where your items ended up. After removal, check in with the crew about disposal. Reputable operators can tell you which pieces were donated, recycled, or sent to a transfer facility. Since 75% of customers now prioritize eco-friendly disposal when choosing a provider, this is a fair and reasonable question to ask every time.

Ready to Clear Out? Here Is What to Do Next

You have already done the hard work of reading through this guide, so let the key points sink in before you do anything else. Know what items qualify, lock in a firm upfront quote, run the real numbers before assuming DIY is cheaper, and confirm that your provider recycles or donates before booking. Those four steps alone will save you time, money, and a few headaches.

Hampton Roads homeowners, landlords, military families, and contractors all have a local option that handles furniture removal alongside demolition and full property cleanouts under one roof. No need to call a hauler for the sofa, a separate demo crew for the old cabinets, and a third vendor for the debris. Mr. Demo Pro covers all of it, serving Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, Newport News, Hampton, Suffolk, and surrounding areas.

Same-day and next-day availability means there is no reason to let that old sectional sit in your driveway for another month collecting water damage or drawing HOA attention. When you are ready, call Mr. Demo Pro at 757-848-4559 or request a free estimate online for a transparent, no-surprise quote. The crew is ready when you are.

Conclusion

Getting rid of old furniture in Hampton Roads does not have to be a stressful experience. By understanding how pricing works, knowing what removal companies will and won't accept, and planning your pickup in advance, you can turn a frustrating chore into a quick and painless process. Choosing the right service also means your unwanted pieces may find a second life through donation or recycling rather than ending up in a landfill.

Now that you know what to expect, you are ready to take action. Start by gathering a list of the items you need removed, then reach out to a reputable Hampton Roads junk removal company for a quote. The sooner you make that call, the sooner you can reclaim your space and finally enjoy a clutter-free home. Your fresh start is just one phone call away.

structuredData.articleBody:
So you've got an old couch taking up half your living room, a broken dresser that's been sitting in the corner for months, or maybe an entire room full of furniture you just don't need anymore. Sound familiar? You're definitely not alone. Getting rid of bulky furniture is one of those tasks that feels way more complicated than it should be.

That's where junk furniture removal services come in, and if you live in the Hampton Roads area, you've got some solid options available to you. But before you grab your phone and start calling around, there are a few things worth knowing that can save you time, money, and a whole lot of headaches.

Whether you're clearing out after a move, downsizing, or just finally tackling that cluttered spare room, this guide is here to help. We're breaking down eight important things every Hampton Roads homeowner should understand before scheduling a pickup. From pricing to what companies will and won't take, consider this your beginner-friendly roadmap to getting that unwanted furniture out of your life for good.

What Actually Counts as Junk Furniture

Before you schedule a pickup, it helps to know exactly what falls under the junk furniture removal umbrella. The good news is that most of the bulky stuff cluttering your home qualifies without any problem.

Standard accepted items cover a wide range, including sofas, sectionals, recliners, loveseats, mattresses, box springs, bed frames, dressers, dining tables and chairs, desks, office chairs, bookshelves, entertainment centers, and outdoor patio furniture. If it used to serve a purpose in your home and it no longer does, there's a strong chance a removal crew can haul it away in a single visit.

Large appliances are a bit of a gray area. Refrigerators, washers, dryers, and dishwashers often fall within the scope of furniture removal services, but you should always confirm before scheduling. Refrigerators and freezers containing Freon may require special handling prior to transport, which can affect pricing. According to Waste Management's household hazardous waste guidance, certain materials require care beyond standard collection, so a quick call to confirm appliance acceptance saves you from surprises on removal day.

What crews will not take includes hazardous materials such as paint, chemicals, asbestos-containing materials, propane tanks, and medical waste. The EPA classifies products like paints, cleaners, oils, and pesticides as household hazardous waste requiring specialized disposal, which falls completely outside standard junk removal.

One of the biggest perks of professional junk furniture removal is the ability to combine items into a single service call. A broken sofa, an old dresser, and a stack of patio chairs can all go out the door at once, saving you from scheduling multiple pickups.

How Junk Furniture Removal Is Priced in Hampton Roads

Pricing is one of the first things people want to know before scheduling a pickup, and the good news is that it's pretty straightforward once you understand how the system works.

Most professional junk removal companies price by volume, meaning the amount of space your items take up in the truck. It's not typically charged by the hour or by how many individual pieces you have. A single heavy recliner might cost less than a lightweight but bulky sectional that eats up half the truck, simply because the sectional takes up more space.

Here's a realistic look at what junk furniture removal costs in the Hampton Roads area:

  • Single large item (one sofa, mattress, or dresser): roughly $75 to $150

  • Partial truckload (a few pieces of furniture, like a bedroom set or a couch plus a couple of chairs): approximately $150 to $300

  • Full truckload: generally $400 to $600, depending on item weight and local disposal fees

According to how much junk removal costs in Hampton Roads, labor alone represents 42% of total junk removal expenses industry-wide. That's a big chunk, and it's one reason why pricing can vary so much from one provider to another. It also explains why some companies surprise customers with extra charges after the truck is already loaded.

Some national franchise operators use variable or tiered fee structures that aren't fully disclosed until the crew shows up. Local providers who offer free, itemized estimates give you a firm number before any work begins, which protects your budget from unexpected add-ons.

The easiest way to know your actual cost before committing? Request a free estimate. Send a few photos of your items or schedule a quick walkthrough call. Mr. Demo Pro offers free estimates for furniture removal throughout Hampton Roads, including Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, and Newport News. You can reach them at 757-848-4559 to get a clear, upfront quote with no surprises.

DIY vs. Professional Removal: The Real Cost Breakdown

A lot of homeowners assume DIY is the obvious budget move when it comes to junk furniture removal. But once you run the actual numbers, that assumption starts to fall apart pretty quickly.

Renting a pickup truck or cargo van in Hampton Roads typically runs $80 to $130 per day before you add mileage charges and fuel. Mileage fees alone can run $0.70 to $1.10 per mile, and a loaded truck gets rough gas mileage. Here's the part most people miss: a typical furniture haul, think a sofa, mattress, dresser, and a few chairs, usually fills more than one load. That means at least two trips to a landfill or transfer station, and every trip adds to your total.

Virginia tipping fees for bulky waste range from $25 to $60 per visit depending on the facility and how much your load weighs. Two trips means doubling that estimate. Most people budget for one and get surprised at the scale house.

There's also a real physical risk that doesn't show up on any receipt. Back strains and crush injuries from moving heavy furniture are among the most common home-related injuries. Standard homeowners insurance policies typically do not cover accidents that happen during DIY moving or hauling, so an ER visit lands entirely on you.

On top of all that, not every Hampton Roads transfer station accepts mattresses or large upholstered furniture on the same day or at the same location. You may need to call ahead, drive to a separate facility, or wait for a scheduled bulky waste day.

When you stack up truck rental, fuel, tipping fees (times two), and a half-day of your time, professional removal often comes in within $50 to $100 of the DIY total. Check out this 2026 junk removal cost breakdown by state to see how the numbers compare in your region. The professional option skips the heavy lifting, the logistics, and the guesswork entirely.

Eco-Friendly Disposal: Where Your Furniture Actually Goes

Here's something worth knowing before you book any removal service: eco-friendly disposal is a genuine purchase driver for most people today. North America leads the global junk removal market largely because of high consumer awareness and demand for green services, and reputable haulers have responded by building real sorting systems into their process.

The Disposal Hierarchy That Responsible Haulers Follow

The best operators follow a clear sequence after your furniture leaves the curb. Usable items go to donation partners first, recyclable materials go to processors second, and only items with absolutely no remaining life end up in a landfill. According to the U.S. EPA, Americans send roughly 146 million tons of waste to landfills every year, which is exactly why this sorting step matters so much.

Where Your Furniture Goes Locally

In Hampton Roads, furniture in good condition gets routed to donation partners like Habitat for Humanity ReStores, with locations across Norfolk, Virginia Beach, and Chesapeake, and Salvation Army, both of which resell furniture to fund community programs. For pieces that cannot be donated, material recycling takes over. Metal frames go to scrap processors, wood components move to appropriate waste streams, and foam and fabric are handled by facilities equipped for upholstered materials.

The Question You Should Always Ask

Ask any hauler directly about their disposal chain: which donation partners they use, their recycling rate, and what percentage actually reaches a landfill. Reputable companies should answer this without hesitation. Since no hauler is legally required to report diversion rates and most figures are self-reported, asking directly is simply smart consumer behavior.

Virginia-Specific Rules for Mattresses and Regulated Items

Not all furniture removal is created equal, and Virginia has its own set of rules that can catch homeowners off guard if they're not prepared. Here are five things you need to know before hauling anything to the curb.

1. Mattresses Have Curbside Restrictions in Hampton Roads

Virginia has no statewide mattress recycling mandate, but individual cities handle this differently. In many Hampton Roads municipalities, you cannot simply drag a mattress to the curb and expect it to disappear. Unpermitted curbside mattress placement can trigger a code violation fine, so always contact your city's public works department to schedule a bulky item pickup before putting anything outside.

2. Electronics Cannot Go Into Standard Removal Loads

Smart TVs, built-in speakers, and similar electronics embedded in furniture setups fall under Virginia's Electronic Waste Recycling Act. These items require separate handling through dedicated programs. The Southeastern Public Service Authority's HHW and E-Waste facilities serve Hampton Roads residents, though drop-offs are capped at five items per visit and require proof of residence. The Virginia DEQ's Universal Waste Requirements govern these disposal obligations at the state level.

3. Appliances With Refrigerants Require Certified Handling

Refrigerators and AC units contain refrigerants that must be recovered by an EPA Section 608-certified technician before disposal. Always confirm your removal provider holds this certification before booking.

4. Pre-1978 Homes May Have Lead Paint or Asbestos

Furniture and composite materials from older renovations may contain lead paint or asbestos. Both fall entirely outside standard junk removal scope and require professional assessment before anyone hauls anything away.

5. Licensing Protects You From Liability

If a regulated item in your load is later found to have been improperly disposed of, liability can fall back on you as the property owner in a DIY scenario. Using a licensed, insured company like Mr. Demo Pro removes that risk entirely. Call 757-848-4559 for a free estimate.

Military PCS Moves Keep the Volume High

Naval Station Norfolk is one of the largest naval installations in the world, and Joint Base Langley-Eustis adds thousands more service members to the local population. When PCS orders arrive, they typically give families weeks, not months, to relocate. Selling furniture online takes time you don't have. Donation centers often require drop-offs during limited hours. Professional furniture removal becomes the fastest, most practical solution when the clock is already running.

Rental Turnovers Create Repeat Business

Hampton Roads has a dense and active rental market, partly because military families tend to rent rather than buy. When a tenant moves out, landlords need the unit cleared fast to minimize vacancy time. Abandoned sofas, broken bed frames, and worn-out appliances don't move themselves, and property managers can't wait days for piecemeal pickups.

When a family member passes away or transitions to assisted living, the resulting cleanout often involves an entire household worth of furniture. Families coordinating from out of town especially benefit from a single comprehensive service call rather than managing multiple vendors.
